correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the complete published 48-line list, derives all same-family and cross-family incidences by solving linear equations, and constructs the entire adjacency matrix over integers. Exact enumeration gives degree \(14\) and \(336\) edges; exact characteristic-polynomial calculation gives \((t-14)(t-2)^{28}(t+2)^{12}(t+6)^6(t+10)\). For skew pairs, entries of \(A^2\) count common Fermat-line transversals and exhaust all \(792\) pairs with profile \(2:96,4:192,6:480,10:24\). The K3 intersection formula \(G=A-2I\) then gives rank \(20\) and inertia \((1,19,28)\).

value.rationale: The Fermat quartic is a canonical Picard-rank-\(20\) K3 surface and its 48-line configuration is a standard benchmark in the geometry of line-rich quartics. The full spectrum refines the familiar rank-\(20\) fact to an exact integral decomposition, while the skew-pair profile measures a natural projective incidence invariant for every nonintersecting pair. The calculation therefore links the finite line configuration directly to the Néron–Severi intersection form rather than selecting an arbitrary slice.
